excluded_vuln_classes: Clickjacking on pages with no sensitive actions
CSRF on unauthenticated forms or forms without confidential actions
Rate limiting/brute force on unauthenticated endpoints
Missing security headers / CSP / HttpOnly / Secure cookie flags
Version/banner disclosure, descriptive error messages/stack traces
Open redirect without additional demonstrated impact
Self-XSS / DOM XSS without clear impact
Content/privacy-policy discrepancies (route to Unico's DPO instead)
Broken links/typos/content issues on static/marketing pages
policy_notes: Two distinct scopes: PRIMARY = Liveness (biometric presentation-attack bypass -- Photo/Video-Replay/3D-Mask/Deepfake attacks against the SDK, must achieve 'live:true'). SECONDARY = Web (standard XSS/RCE/SQLi/SSRF/JWT/IDOR/file-upload classes on the URL list above).

Liveness scope requires PHYSICAL mobile devices (Android/iOS) or a browser with camera access -- mobile apps explicitly do NOT work on emulators/simulators. Not pursuing this scope from this sandboxed environment; would need the user's own phone/camera, out of this session's recon-only remit.
Liveness reports must include Transaction ID + Process ID; testing focuses on the biometric SDK/engine, NOT the wrapper test apps (wrapper/presentation-layer issues explicitly out of scope).

Web scope IDOR requires 'accessing confidential information from another user/organization' -- needs an authenticated account context to demonstrate; most of Web scope realistically needs authenticated testing beyond what this pass can do without an account (per user's standing no-account-creation rule).
Program explicitly requests 'X-HackerOne-Research: [H1 username]' AND 'User-Agent: [H1 username]' headers on all requests.
Employees/former employees/first-degree relatives/third parties with confidential access are excluded from participating (not relevant to us).
Extremely fresh -- launched Jan 2026, only 26 resolved reports as of this hunt.

Given the narrow Web scope (mostly exact URLs, not broad wildcards) and heavy exclusion list (no takeover, no version/banner disclosure, no header/TLS hygiene), the realistic unauthenticated-recon angle is narrower than prior programs: DNS private-IP disclosure sweep (not excluded) and cloud/bucket enum (not excluded) are the best-fit passive techniques; standard config-exposure/secrets-in-JS checks also still apply.
